There is a very recognizable genre on the German web: a letter that looks like concern for your website, but in reality sells a service through anxiety.

The most common formula is: "You do not have a cookie banner, which means your website is violating the law".
It sounds confident. But this is exactly where oversimplification usually begins.

A banner is not required "always", but under a specific site config: trackers, analytics, external services, embeds. If those are not present, the question looks different.

I.e. why the appropriate response is not panic, but a review of the facts: what is actually loading, what requires consent, what is already described in the privacy section.

In the article, I examine not only the legal framework, but also the mechanism of such letters itself. Because the problem is often not compliance, but how the market monetizes uncertainty through fear. 🧩
